title: Initial-vertex restriction of join slices fixes arbitrary boundary data
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, nerves, simplicial subsets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and joins and the join-slice construction of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], and trivial Kan fibrations of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Let $T$ be a small partially ordered set with a least element $t$, let $\mathcal E$ be a quasicategory, let $\mathcal E_0\subseteq\mathcal E$ be a full subcategory, and let $p:N(T)\to\mathcal E$ be a diagram, all in fixed containing universes. For any small simplicial set $K$ and diagram $q:K\to\mathcal E$, write $\mathcal E_{/q}$ for the join slice, whose $n$-simplices are maps $\Delta^n\star K\to\mathcal E$ restricting to $q$ on $K$, with source projection to $\mathcal E$ given by the entire initial face. Put $\mathcal E_{0,/q}=\mathcal E_0\times_{\mathcal E}\mathcal E_{/q}$. Restriction along $\{t\}\hookrightarrow N(T)$ induces a trivial Kan fibration
$$r:\mathcal E_{0,/p}\longrightarrow\mathcal E_{0,/p(t)}$$
over $\mathcal E_0$. Explicitly, for every inclusion of simplicial sets $L\subseteq M$, every $h:L\to\mathcal E_{0,/p}$ and every $v:M\to\mathcal E_{0,/p(t)}$ with $rh=v|_L$, there exists $\widetilde v:M\to\mathcal E_{0,/p}$ with $\widetilde v|_L=h$ and $r\widetilde v=v$. Thus the entire prescribed boundary and every source simplex are fixed. No limits or colimits in $\mathcal E$ or $\mathcal E_0$ are assumed.

source.place: Dual of Proposition 2.1.2.5, printed p.62 (PDF p.79), with π:E→Δ⁰ and the left-anodyne inclusion {t}→N(T); the initial-vertex instance is used explicitly in Proposition 5.3.5.15, proof (a), printed p.411 (PDF p.428). Restricting the sources is base change over E. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this join-slice lifting theorem.

proof.text: Put $P=T^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $B=N(P)$. Define reversal of a simplicial set by $(X^{\mathrm{op}})_n=X_n$ and $X^{\mathrm{op}}(\alpha)=X(\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}})$, where $\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}(j)=n-\alpha(m-j)$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$. Reversing a chain identifies $B^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $N(T)$. From the ordered-block formula for joins, reversing the blocks gives $(X\star Y)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong Y^{\mathrm{op}}\star X^{\mathrm{op}}$: a mixed simplex $(x\in X_u,y\in Y_v)$ is sent to $(y,x)$ with the reversed operators. These identifications commute with maps and preserve pure-factor faces.

source.place: Elementary ordered-block reversal preparing the opposite of Proposition 4.3.6.4.

proof.text: The vertex $t$ is greatest in $P$. For $i:\{t\}\hookrightarrow B$, [lem-coef-infinity-cone-mono-right-anodyne] makes $e=i\star\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^0}:\{t\}^{\triangleright}\hookrightarrow B^{\triangleright}$ right anodyne. Let $a:\{t\}\to\{t\}^{\triangleright}$ and $b:B\to B^{\triangleright}$ be base inclusions, and let $q:\{t\}^{\triangleright}\to\{t\}$ be constant. Define $G:B^{\triangleright}\to B$ by sending the new cone vertex to $t$ and each old vertex to itself: on a chain ending in the new vertex, replace that vertex by $t$. This is a simplicial map since every element of $P$ is at most $t$; repetitions produce degenerate chains. Then $Gb=\operatorname{id}_B$ and $qa=\operatorname{id}_{\{t\}}$. The pairs $(a,b):i\to e$ and $(q,G):e\to i$ are arrow maps since $ea=bi$ and $Ge=iq$, and their composite is the identity. Thus $i$ is a retract of $e$, and is right anodyne by the retract closure in the cited statement.

source.place: Corollary 4.7.3.22, (2) to (3), explicit retract for the nerve of a poset; cone input is Lemma 4.3.7.8 (0196).

proof.text:
For the arbitrary inclusion $L\hookrightarrow M$, apply the pushout-join clause of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] to $i:\{t\}\hookrightarrow B$ from Step 2 and $L^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow M^{\mathrm{op}}$. It gives an inner anodyne inclusion from $(\{t\}\star M^{\mathrm{op}})\amalg_{\{t\}\star L^{\mathrm{op}}}(B\star L^{\mathrm{op}})$ to $B\star M^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversal changes the horn $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$; hence it preserves inner horns. It preserves pushouts, transfinite compositions and retract diagrams because it only reindexes simplicial operators and leaves the sets in each degree unchanged. The weakly saturated inner-anodyne class in that cited statement is therefore preserved. Applying Step 1 identifies the reversed inclusion with
$$j:D=(L\star N(T))\amalg_{L\star\{t\}}(M\star\{t\})\hookrightarrow M\star N(T),$$
so $j$ is inner anodyne. Both hypotheses of the cited join clause hold: $i$ is right anodyne and the second map is degreewise injective.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, right-anodyne first-variable clause, with explicit reversal to the left-anodyne second-variable clause.

proof.text: For any simplicial set $A$, the definition in [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] identifies maps $A\to\mathcal E_{/p}$ with maps $A\star N(T)\to\mathcal E$ restricting to $p$ on $N(T)$. Explicitly, from $f:A\to\mathcal E_{/p}$, send a mixed simplex $(a\in A_u,z\in N(T)_v)$ to the value of $f_u(a):\Delta^u\star N(T)\to\mathcal E$ on the mixed simplex $(\operatorname{id}_{[u]},z)$; on the pure $N(T)$ summand use $p$, and on the pure $A$ summand use the source of $f$. Conversely, restrict the join map along $\sigma\star\operatorname{id}$ for each $\sigma:\Delta^n\to A$. The displayed simplicial operators make these constructions inverse and compatible with restriction. The pullback defining $\mathcal E_{0,/p}$ adds exactly a source map $A\to\mathcal E_0$ whose composite with $\mathcal E_0\hookrightarrow\mathcal E$ is the pure $A$ restriction.

source.place: Join-slice definition carried by lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration; explicit mixed-simplex verification of its parameter interpretation.

proof.text: By Step 4, $h$ gives $H:L\star N(T)\to\mathcal E$ over $p$, and $v$ gives $V:M\star\{t\}\to\mathcal E$ over $p(t)$. The identity $rh=v|_L$ says exactly $H|_{L\star\{t\}}=V|_{L\star\{t\}}$, including pure $L$ faces and higher simplices. Hence $H$ and $V$ define $w:D\to\mathcal E$ on the pushout in Step 3. Concretely, its degreewise union has intersection $L\star\{t\}$, as seen by intersecting pure and mixed summands of the join formula. It contains all of $N(T)$ and all of $M$, and $w$ equals $p$ on the first and the source of $v$ on the second. This remains valid when $L$ or $M$ is empty, since $\varnothing\star N(T)=N(T)$.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.5 proof, printed pp.62-63: translate lifting data into the pushout join; here with reversed orientation and arbitrary parameter inclusion.

proof.text: The quasicategory condition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] extends a map into $\mathcal E$ across every inner horn. The class of maps across which every map into $\mathcal E$ extends contains isomorphisms and is closed under the operations defining inner anodyne maps in [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones]: across a pushout, extend on the attached summand and glue; along a transfinite composition, choose compatible extensions at successor stages and take their degreewise union at a limit stage; for an arrow retract $u\to u'\to u$, precompose the given domain map with the domain retraction, extend across $u'$, and restrict along the codomain section. Therefore $w$ extends across the inner anodyne $j$ of Step 3 to $W:M\star N(T)\to\mathcal E$.

source.place: Inner-anodyne weak saturation, with the lifting-class closure argument supplied explicitly.

proof.text: The extension $W$ equals $p$ on $N(T)$, equals $H$ on $L\star N(T)$, and equals $V$ on $M\star\{t\}$. Under the inverse construction of Step 4 it gives $\widetilde v:M\to\mathcal E_{/p}$ with $\widetilde v|_L=h$ and $r\widetilde v=v$. Its pure $M$ restriction is exactly the source map of $v$, which already factors through $\mathcal E_0$; pair this same source map with $\widetilde v$ in the defining pullback to obtain $M\to\mathcal E_{0,/p}$. Thus every source simplex and the entire prescribed boundary are fixed, with no need to infer membership from vertices.

source.place: Dual of Proposition 2.1.2.5; pullback restriction of the source, as used in Proposition 5.3.5.15(a).

proof.text: Steps 3--7 solve the stated lifting problem for every inclusion $L\subseteq M$. Taking $L=\varnothing$ and $M=\Delta^0$ proves vertex surjectivity. Taking $L=\partial\Delta^n$ and $M=\Delta^n$ for each $n\geq1$ proves all the other lifting clauses of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Hence $r$ is a trivial Kan fibration over $\mathcal E_0$. The construction uses only simplicial sets, the least-element property, and inner horn filling in $\mathcal E$; it assumes no limits or colimits in $\mathcal E$ or $\mathcal E_0$.

source.place: Tag 08NL, label definition-trivial-kan; dimension zero is vertex surjectivity.
